$q_{in}[m^{3}/s]$ - water inflow
$q_{out}[m^{3}/s]$ - water outflow
$h[m]$ - water level
$A[m^{2}]$ - cross section

Balance of water volume
$V[m^{3}]$ - water volume
$\boxed{\frac{dV}{dt}=q_{in}-q_{out}}$
Transformations for practical reasons
More terminology
$V=A·h$
$A· \frac{dh}{dt}=q_{in}-q_{out}$
- state variables -  h 
- input (control) variables - $q_{in}$ , $q_{out}$
- output variables - h
- disturbances - $q_{in}$ , $q_{out}$ (rain,evaporation)
- parameters - A
# 2 heating system of a house
Balance of thermal energy $E[J]$
$Q_{out}=k(T-T_{out}) \ [J/s]$ Flow of energy leaving house
$\frac{dE}{dt}=Q_{in}-Q_{out} \ [J/s]$ Energy balance

state - $T$
input - $Q_{in}$
output - $T$
distrurbance - $T_{out}$
parameters - $C,k$

ideal mixing
2 liquids $A,B$
2 balances
$V_{A}[m^{3}]$ - volume of liquid A
$V_{B}[m^{3}]$ - volume of liquid B
Mixture - concetrations
$C_{A}=\frac{V_{A}}{V_{A}+V_{B}}$
$C_{B}=\frac{V_{B}}{V_{A}+V_{B}}$
$\begin{cases}\frac{dV_{A}}{dt}=q_{A}-C_{A}q_{0} \\  \frac{dV_{B}}{dt}=q_{B}-C_{B}q_{0}\end{cases}$
transformations
$V_{A}=S·h·C_{A}$
$V_{B}=S·h·C_{B}$
State variables: $h,C_{A}$
Input: $q_{A},q_{B},q_{out}$
Outputs: $h,C_{A}$
Parameters: $S$

---
state equasions
state-space equasions
state-space model
$V_{A}=h·S·C_{A}$
$V_{B}=h·S(1-C_{A})$
$C_{A=\frac{V_{A}}{V_{A}+V_{B}}}$


$\begin{cases}\frac{dV_{A}}{dt}=q_{A}-C_{A}·q_{0} \\  \frac{dV_{B}}{dt}=q_{B}-(1-C_{A})·q_{0}\end{cases}$

$\begin{cases}S\frac{d}{dt}(h·C_{A})=q_{A}-C_{A}·q_{0} \\  S\frac{d}{dt}h( 1-C_{A})=q_{B}-(1-C_{A})·q_{0}\end{cases}$
State variables: $h,C_{A}$

$\begin{cases}S \frac{dh}{dt}=q_{A}+q_{B}-q_{0} \\  Sh \frac{dC_{A}}{dt}+C_{A}(q_{A}+q_{B}-\cancel{ q_{0} })=q_{A}-\cancel{ C_{A}Q_{0} }\end{cases}$

$\begin{cases}S \frac{dh}{dt}=q_{A}+q_{B}-q_{0} \\  Sh \frac{dC_{A}}{dt}=q_{a}-C_{A}(q_{a}+q_{b})\end{cases}$

$\text{state equasions}\begin{cases}h=\frac{1}{s}(q_{A}+q_{B}-q_{0}) \\  C_{A}=\frac{1}{sh}[q_{A}-C_{A}(q_{A}+q_{B})]\end{cases}$

Balance of forces
$m_{1}\ddot{x}_{1}+D_{1}(\dot{x}_{1}-\dot{x}_{2})+K_{1}x_{1}=F_{1}$
$m_{2}\ddot{x}_{2}-D_{1}(\dot{x}_{1}-\dot{x}_{2})+D_{2}\dot{x}_{2}+K_{2}x_{2}=F_{2}$

State equasions:
$\dot{x}_{1}=v_{1}$
$\dot{v}_{1}=\frac{1}{m_{1}}[F_{1}-D_{1}(v_{1}-v_{2})-K_{1}x_{1}]$
$\dot{x}_{2}=v_{2}$
$\dot{v}_{2}=\frac{1}{m_{2}}[F_{2}+D_{1}(v_{1}-v_{2})-D_{2}v_{2}-K_{2}x_{2}]$

Balance of forces
$\text{"}x_{1}\text{"}: \ Kx_{1}+D(\dot{x}_{1}-\dot{x}_{2})=0$
$\text{"}x_{2}\text{"}=m·\ddot{x}_{2}+D(\dot{x}_{2}-\dot{x}_{1})=F$

Change to state space model
State variables:
$x_{1},x_{2},v_{2}$
$\dot{x}_{1}=\frac{1}{D}(-Kx_{1}+v_{2})$
$\dot{x}_{2}=v_{2}$

$\dot{v}_{2}=\frac{1}{m}[F-D(v_{2}-\dot{x}_{1})]$
derivative can only be on the left side
$\dot{v}_{2}=\frac{1}{m}\left[ F-D\left( v_{2}-\frac{1}{D}(-Kx_{1}+V_{2}) \right) \right]$

How can we be sure/convinced about correctness of our modeling

Law of equal signs
all variables should  have equal signs to not explode to infinity
start from simple systems
Passivity
equasion going to infinity is bad
in a system with no external sources of energy the value must tend to 0
